help.intro: A text of about 200 words about the German weather in records: the hottest day ever measured (41.2 degrees, in 2019), the coldest place (a small lake in the Alps where it reached minus 45.9), the sunniest city, the rainiest region and the mountain where snow lies seven months a year. It also explains why Germans talk about the weather so much and what Aprilwetter means. All facts are real and were checked. You read what you have just learnt: the weather words (es regnet, es schneit, die Sonne scheint, bewölkt, der Grad) and the comparative (heißer als, kälter als, am wärmsten, mehr als, so viel wie). Read for the gist first, then find one number or one place per question.
help.tips[0].title: Comparing: -er als, am -sten
help.tips[0].text: Comparative: adjective + -er + als: Freiburg ist wärmer als Hamburg. Short adjectives with a, o, u take an umlaut: warm → wärmer, kalt → kälter, groß → größer, jung → jünger. Irregular: gut → besser, viel → mehr, gern → lieber, hoch → höher. Superlative: am + -sten: am wärmsten, am kältesten, am meisten, am höchsten. Equal: so warm wie, genauso viel wie.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: In the south it is warmer than in the north, but by the sea it rains less than in the Alps.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: It was coldest at the Funtensee: minus 45.9 degrees.
help.tips[0].check.q: Der Juli ist ____ als der Mai. (warm)
help.tips[0].check.why: warm takes an umlaut in the comparative: wärmer als.
help.tips[1].text: Es regnet (it rains), es schneit (it snows), die Sonne scheint, es ist bewölkt (cloudy), es ist windig, es ist neblig (foggy), es gewittert (there is a thunderstorm). Temperatures: 20 Grad, minus 5 Grad, plus 30 Grad. Nouns: der Regen, der Schnee, die Sonne, die Wolke, der Wind, der Nebel, das Gewitter, die Hitze (heat), die Kälte (cold). Aprilwetter: sun, rain, snow and sun again in one day; Germans use it for anything that changes all the time.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: In April the sun shines, then it rains, then it snows, and then the sun shines again.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: On the Zugspitze snow lies seven months a year.
help.tips[1].check.why: bewölkt = cloudy (Wolke = cloud); neblig = foggy; es gewittert = thunderstorm.

help.remember[1]: Es regnet, es schneit, die Sonne scheint, bewölkt, neblig; 20 Grad, minus 5 Grad.
help.exam: Short factual texts about weather and climate with numbers and comparisons are a typical reading task at this level.
help.hook: 41.2 degrees in the north, minus 45.9 in a mountain lake, snow for seven months: read Germany's weather records and why everyone here talks about the weather.
help.vocab[4].example: Rügen hat fast 2.000 Sonnenstunden im Jahr.
passageTranslation:
Germans like talking about the weather. No wonder: it changes often. In April the sun shines, then it rains, then it snows, and in the afternoon the sun shines again. That is called Aprilwetter, April weather.

The climate is mild. In summer it is mostly 20 to 25 degrees, in winter between minus 5 and plus 5 degrees. But there are records. The hottest day was on 25 July 2019: in Duisburg and in Tönisvorst, both in the west, 41.2 degrees were measured. Before that it had never been so hot in Germany.

The coldest place is the Funtensee in the Alps, a small lake in a valley. There it was minus 45.9 degrees in December 2001. That is colder than in Moscow and as cold as in Siberia! The lake lies in a hollow, and the cold air cannot escape.

It is warmest in the south-west, in Freiburg and on the Upper Rhine. The island of Rügen in the Baltic Sea has the most sun: almost 2,000 hours of sunshine a year. The most rain falls in the Alps. Hamburg has a bad reputation, but it rains less there than in Munich, only more often.

The highest mountain is the Zugspitze, 2,962 metres. On top snow lies seven months a year, and in summer it is colder there than in winter in Hamburg.
